answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in slow, verifiable history: each identity earns standing only by completing attested work over time, like a lotus that opens one petal per season and cannot be rushed. A public beacon publishes the reputation ledger so peers can check an agent's record before paying it, while a quill-signed audit trail ties every transaction to that history. New identities start with tiny limits and rising collateral, so creating thousands of fakes costs more than the fraud could ever return.
